rows.name: spoken-why-warps-frozen-5
rows.question: Why
rows.answer: Because a warp shares instruction-issue resources, threads are most efficient when they execute the same instructions together. If they take different branches, the GPU generally executes each path with only the relevant threads active, leaving other lanes idle. Accessing consecutive memory locations also helps because the GPU can combine those accesses into fewer memory transactions.

rows.name: spoken-why-during-coding-frozen-21
rows.question: Y
rows.answer: A circular array gives the FIFO a fixed capacity of exactly 17, with constant-time push and pop and no shifting of elements. Tracking the head and element count distinguishes empty from full, so all 17 slots are usable and an overflow push can fail without changing the queue. Advancing indices modulo 17 reuses freed slots while preserving FIFO order; the wraparound test checks that boundary behavior.

rows.question: Y
rows.answer: Interpreting “Y” as “why”: “unreliable” describes the customer’s experience, but not which part of the service is failing. Tracing affected orders and measuring specific failures helps distinguish delivery delays from refill errors or misleading updates, so we don’t fix the wrong problem. Safety risks and customers running out of essential supplies come first; after that, prioritize recurring failures by severity and how many customers they affect.
